newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian stocks take a break, mood positive.
newsitem.headline: Austrian stocks take a break, mood positive.

text.p: Austrian shares finished the week on a weaker note after a quiet trading day, taking a breather after Thursday's unsuccessful attempt to break a six-year old historic high in the blue-chip ATX index.
The ATX closed down 6.35 points or 0.51 percent at 1,244.01. Among its constituents, 17 shares fell, three rose and one remained unchanged.
"There was a bit of uncertainty after the U.S. payroll data, but now it looks like the positive scenario is holding," said a trader. "The data ended up being a bit of a non-event."

Market participants said they expected the index to remain trapped in a narrow range between 1,240 and 1,260, adding a new attempt at breaking the all-time high of 1,257.96 -- reached in April 1991 -- could not be ruled out.
Analysts at Creditanstalt Investmentbank said earlier on Friday they expected the ATX to rise to 1,280 by year-end but wanred that they saw strong technical resistance at 1,250 points.
Decliners were led by brewery group BBAG, falling 1.32 percent to close at 743. Steel maker Boehler led the handful of gainers, inching up 0.75 percent to 831 schillings.
